title: automate tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform)
author: Priya Menon
body:
Motivation: Private deployments require an automated, idempotent RBAC bootstrap that works across the Private installer (Helm-based), the Terraform tenant modules, and upgrade/rollback flows. Today teams perform manual role creation or run ad-hoc scripts after installation which causes drift during upgrades and slows onboarding. This PR implements a unified automation flow that: 1) provides a namespaced tenant bootstrap Job for Helm installs; 2) exposes a Terraform hook for preflight role provisioning when using the Terraform tenant module; 3) tightens the RBAC roles to least privilege for bootstrap operations; and 4) adds explicit upgrade/rollback-safe annotations so the installer can re-run bootstraps without creating duplicates.

Changes (summary): 
- Add a new Helm template templates/bootstrap-job.yaml which runs a short-lived controller to create tenant-specific Roles and RoleBindings (tenant-admin, tenant-reader, service-account bindings). The Job is idempotent and annotated with install.redwood.com/bootstrap-id to prevent duplicate actions.
- Introduce a Helm values section values.bootstrap.enabled/saName/ttl to control behavior and RBAC scope.
- Terraform: add a new module tests/terraform/tenant-bootstrap-hook that can call the same bootstrap Job via the Kubernetes provider (kubernetes_job) as an optional preflight. This allows infra-as-code installs to ensure roles exist before other resources are applied.
- RBAC policy bundle: add least-privilege Role YAMLs for tenant bootstrap operations and a minimal ClusterRole for the installer controller to reconcile Jobs across namespaces.
- Installer: add idempotency and retry logic in the helm/chart post-render hook; ensure the job uses a Kubernetes TTL controller so finished Jobs are cleaned up automatically.
- Upgrade/rollback: add annotations and a new helper script scripts/rollback/ensure-bootstrap-cleanup.sh used by the private-installer to safely roll back bootstrap state if an upgrade fails.
- Tests & docs: e2e test harness updates in perf-canary to run a simulated tenant bootstrap, and docs/privatedeploy/rbac-bootstrap.md describing config knobs and migration steps.

Why this design: Using a Namespaced Job keeps the bootstrap scoped to the tenant namespace and avoids giving cluster-admin rights to customer-managed controllers. The Terraform hook mirrors the Helm flow so both IaC and Helm users get identical RBAC state. The annotative idempotency avoids race conditions during concurrent installs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add Helm template and values
- [x] Add Terraform hook module + example
- [x] Add RBAC policy YAMLs (tenant Roles + installer ClusterRole)
- [x] Add e2e test case in perf-canary
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Security review sign-off (see reviewer thread)

Testing notes: 
- Local Helm install tested against Kind cluster; bootstrap Job succeeds and creates expected Roles/Bindings.
- Terraform example tested with the Kubernetes provider against a staging cluster.
- perf-canary job run validates idempotency by running bootstrap twice (second run is no-op).
- CI initially failed on a flaky e2e test (k8s job timeout); timeout increased and rerun passed.

Migration notes: 
- Existing installations that previously relied on manual role creation are unaffected; operators can enable values.bootstrap.enabled to run automatic bootstrap, or run the provided scripts to create roles once.
- The role names are backward compatible with earlier conventions; this PR consolidates duplicates and removes an unnecessary cluster-wide write permission from the previous bootstrap controller.

Security considerations: 
- Roles are scoped to tenant namespaces except for a single minimal ClusterRole for the installer controller that is restricted to listing/watching Jobs and CRDs necessary for reconciliation.
- KMS/HSM keys are not modified by this PR; bootstrap only sets K8s secrets metadata.

Related: ENG-1824, ENG-1899, SUP-4421

Notes for reviewers: focus on RBAC least-privilege boundaries (templates/rbac/*), Helm idempotency semantics (templates/bootstrap-job.yaml + values schema), and Terraform hook implementation (tests/terraform/tenant-bootstrap-hook).

d4e5f6a: add terraform tenant-bootstrap-hook example and docs
b7c8d9e: add RBAC policy YAMLs and reduce installer cluster permissions
c9d0e1f: add e2e test for idempotency in perf-canary
e2f3g4h: fix flake by increasing job timeout and add TTL cleanup
f5g6h7i: update docs and add rollback helper script
review_comments: Luis Ortega: Please tighten the cluster role API verbs - avoid patch/update on cluster-scoped objects. Can we restrict to list/watch for Jobs and CRDs?
Priya Menon: Updated installer ClusterRole to list/watch only; removed unnecessary cluster-wide patch permissions and documented justification in rbac/README.
Alex Chen: Terraform hook looks good but please add a short timeout and retry backoff to avoid long blocking runs during noisy clusters.
Priya Menon: Added backoff/retry policy and lowered default timeout to 5m. Also added a note in the Terraform example about provider timeouts.
Maya Patel: Security review: roles are scoped appropriately; recommend adding an explicit audit log event for bootstrap completions.
Priya Menon: Added audit annotation to the Job and a small log entry on success.
release_notes: Private: Add automated tenant RBAC bootstrap (Helm + Terraform) to simplify tenant onboarding.
RBAC: Introduce least-privilege tenant Roles and a minimal installer ClusterRole.
Installer: Idempotent bootstrap Job with TTL cleanup and rollback helper script.
